record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.context_brief: Hodge-theoretic classification of cubic fourfold Kuznetsov components
record.original_question: Over the complex numbers, for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds, is equivalence of two such components characterized by the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between their Mukai lattices, analogously to the derived Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces?

evidence.quote: It is then natural to ask whether the same happens

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field of complex numbers. For a smooth cubic fourfold $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$, the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves admits Kuznetsov's semi-orthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X), \mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{O}_X(1), \mathcal{O}_X(2) \rangle,$$
where the admissible subcategory $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is called the Kuznetsov component of $X$. The component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is a 2-Calabi–Yau category whose topological K-theory carries a weight-zero Hodge structure and an even integral lattice (the Mukai lattice) $\widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z})$, abstractly isometric to $U^{\oplus 4} \oplus E_8(-1)^{\oplus 2}$, equipped with a distinguished positive 4-space (giving an orientation of the positive directions).

Any $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence $\Phi : \mathcal{K}u(X) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{K}u(Y)$ between Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds $X$ and $Y$ induces a Hodge isometry
$$\Phi^{\widetilde{H}} : \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathbb{Z})$$
which preserves the orientation of the positive 4-spaces.

Question: Is the converse true? That is, given two smooth complex cubic fourfolds $X$ and $Y$, does the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry
$$\widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(X), \mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{H}(\mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathbb{Z})$$
imply the existence of an exact $\mathbb{C}$-linear equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(X) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y)$, in direct analogy with the derived Torelli theorem of Mukai–Orlov (and its twisted/oriented refinement) for K3 surfaces?
artifact.status_search_result: A derived-Torelli statement for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds — characterizing equivalence of Kuznetsov components by the existence of an orientation-preserving Hodge isometry of Mukai lattices, in analogy with Mukai–Orlov for K3 surfaces — is treated as an open conjecture in the literature. Partial results exist (e.g., for special cubic fourfolds whose Kuznetsov component is equivalent to D^b of a (twisted) K3 surface, where Mukai–Orlov-type theorems apply, and various categorical Torelli theorems), but the general statement has not been established.

status_evidence.title: The K3 category of a cubic fourfold – an update (D. Huybrechts)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the conjectural derived Torelli theorem for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds and its known partial cases.
status_evidence.claim: The analogue of the derived Torelli theorem for Ku(X) of cubic fourfolds is stated as a conjecture, established only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Hodge theory and derived categories of cubic fourfolds (Addington–Thomas)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when Ku(X) is equivalent to D^b of a (twisted) K3 surface in terms of the Mukai-lattice Hodge structure.
status_evidence.claim: Provides supporting lattice/Hodge results for the conjectural categorical/derived Torelli for cubic fourfolds.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the orientation-preserving Hodge-isometry characterization of equivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as open.
